product_family: Computer-vision API and MLS/appraisal products for real estate photo analysis: image tagging/classification, property condition and quality scoring, visual similarity/comparable-property matching, auto-generated captions and descriptions, watermark/duplicate detection, and Photo Compliance (detects logos, yard signs, people, license plates in listing photos). Sold via API and packaged into MLS, AVM/iBuyer, appraisal/inspection, and insurance-focused product lines.

certifications.name: SOC 2 (Type 1/2)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. No trust center exists (restb.ai/security and restb.ai/trust both return 404), and the combined Service & Privacy Policy at restb.ai/terms-conditions/ does not reference SOC 2 in any form.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. The Terms & Conditions describe only 'basic security measures set out in Spanish Royal Decree 1720/2007' and explicitly state 'no higher level measures are available for the Service.' No ISO 27001 or equivalent framework is claimed.

certifications.name: GDPR (posture)
certifications.proof_quote: "This privacy policy is adapted to the Spanish and European regulations and it is compliant with the following rules: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 ... GDPR." and "You appoint us as a data processor of Your Data, to process Your Data on your behalf for the purpose of providing the Service."

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Product is a real estate imagery API; no HIPAA reference anywhere on the vendor's site, and the Terms explicitly prohibit customers from submitting health-related sensitive data through the service.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of a PCI DSS attestation. Not applicable to the product (no payment-card data processed) and not claimed anywhere on the vendor's site.

certifications.name: ISO 27701 / ISO 27017 / ISO 27018
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not mentioned in the Terms & Conditions or anywhere else on the vendor's domain.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management system)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of an AI-governance certification. No AI-specific compliance page exists on the vendor's site.

certifications.name: CSA STAR / CSA STAR AI
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not mentioned anywhere on the vendor's domain.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence, and not applicable — this is a commercial real estate imagery product with no indication of US federal government sales or authorization.

privacy.ai_training_note: The Terms state Restb.ai will 'only process the personal data as specified by these Terms and in accordance with your instructions' and '(d) will not use Your Data for any purposes other than those related to the performance of the Services.' This restricts use of customer data to service delivery but does not explicitly say whether 'performance of the Services' includes using submitted images to improve/retrain the underlying computer-vision models, and there is no opt-out mechanism described. No separate AI-training or model-improvement policy page exists. The training posture is therefore unconfirmed rather than a clear no.
privacy.data_region: Sub-processor Amazon Web Services, Inc., 'with servers in the EU and in the USA, for the purpose of delivering your content (images and metadata) to your end-users.' No dedicated EU-only or US-only hosting option is documented.

security.name: Data processor role (GDPR)
security.value: Restb.ai contractually acts as data processor; customer is data controller.

security.name: Baseline security measures
security.value: "we implement basic security measures set out in Spanish Royal Decree 1720/2007 and no higher level measures are available for the Service." (Note: RD 1720/2007 was the implementing regulation for Spain's pre-GDPR data protection law and was superseded by the LOPDGDD in 2018; this appears to be legacy contract language rather than a current, named security framework.)

security.name: Sub-processors
security.value: Discloses one named sub-processor: Amazon Web Services, Inc. (EU and US servers), used to deliver customer content to end-users.

security.name: Data retention / deletion
security.value: "Upon the expiry or termination of this Agreement or de-registration, or upon request of the Customer, RESTB.AI shall cease any and all use of Your Data and will destroy or return it to you."

security.name: Prohibited data categories
security.value: Terms prohibit customers from submitting special-category/sensitive personal data (racial origin, union membership, religion, ideology, sex life, health, criminal offenses) through the service.

security.name: Warranty disclaimer
security.value: "The products are provided on a strictly 'as is' basis without warranty of any kind."

security.name: Trust center / security page
security.value: Not verified. No trust center; restb.ai/security and restb.ai/trust both return HTTP 404.

compare.pricing_model: Subscription/API-usage based (tiered access to functionality such as automated descriptions and visual similarity search); public pricing not fully disclosed, contact-for-demo model.
compare.data_residency: AWS-hosted, EU and US regions per named sub-processor disclosure; no dedicated data-residency guarantee documented.

flags: No trust center and no SOC 2, ISO 27001, or other third-party security certification was found anywhere on the vendor's domain (restb.ai/security and restb.ai/trust both return 404). For a vendor processing large volumes of MLS/listing imagery at scale, this is a notable gap for prospective enterprise buyers.

The Terms & Conditions cite 'Spanish Royal Decree 1720/2007' as the security baseline and explicitly state 'no higher level measures are available.' RD 1720/2007 predates GDPR and was superseded domestically in 2018, suggesting the legal text may be outdated rather than reflecting current security practice.

AI-training posture on customer imagery is not explicitly confirmed or denied by the vendor; the Terms restrict data use to 'performance of the Services' but do not clarify whether that includes using customer photos to improve the underlying computer-vision models, and no opt-out is documented.
